title: Centering the Margins: Outlier-Based Identification of Harmed Populations in Toxicity Detection
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured model performance disparities (specifically, weighted mean squared error) in toxicity detection for online comments that mention various demographic groups, including religious minorities. It aimed to identify whether models perform worse on text associated with these groups, indicating algorithmic harm.
findings: The study found that comments mentioning religious minorities are disproportionately represented among demographic outliers. Specifically, groups like Hindu and Buddhist had over 50% of their mentions classified as outliers. These outlier groups, which often included religious minorities, experienced higher model error (MSE) in toxicity detection, particularly for identity attacks and severe toxicity. The analysis suggests that harm mitigation efforts should focus on these overrepresented religious groups.
